findings.title: Cross-module acceptance tests have no explicit executable home
findings.location: Section 2 intro under 'Seams'; Section 3 'Acceptance Test Cross-Reference'
findings.evidence: "Per-module test projects test only their own module's internal invariants." / "The following ACC IDs are referenced as never-descopable scope gates."
findings.problem: The document forbids per-module tests from spanning modules but does not define any integration/E2E test project or harness that owns ACC-01/02/03/04/08/10/12.
findings.why_it_matters: The mandatory scope gates cannot be built into CI or verified consistently because they require multiple modules and external dependencies (SolidWorks, WebSocket transport, DB, model client).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a dedicated integration/E2E test project suite, state which ACC IDs it owns, and define its allowed references and runtime dependencies.

findings.title: Timeout recovery is mandatory in Seam B but descopable in Section 3
findings.evidence: "SPEC-03 defines a mandatory post-timeout recovery flow (state refresh or undo-group rollback) before subsequent turns may proceed." / "Descope priority (LIFO): ... error recovery ... all stretch."
findings.problem: The same recovery capability is required for safe continuation after timed-out COM calls and also declared stretch/descopeable.
findings.why_it_matters: If recovery is omitted, later turns may run against mutated but unacknowledged SolidWorks state after a timeout, which breaks correctness and makes lifecycle outcomes untrustworthy.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove timeout recovery from the stretch list or narrow "error recovery" to non-timeout scenarios and explicitly state the mandatory minimum recovery behavior.

findings.title: Grounding tools are simultaneously mandatory and stretch
findings.location: Section 3 'Mandatory vs Stretch (Top-Level)'; Section 3 'Acceptance Test Cross-Reference'
findings.evidence: Mandatory scope includes "`screenshot`, `get_feature_tree`" and ACC-08 is "Screenshot and feature-tree grounding return valid data"; descope says "grounding tools ... all stretch."
findings.problem: The document marks the same functionality as both never-descopable and stretch.
findings.why_it_matters: Scope planning, module specs, and acceptance gating will diverge because implementers cannot tell whether screenshot/feature-tree capabilities are required for the first shippable build.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove screenshot/get_feature_tree from the stretch bucket or redefine "grounding tools" to exclude the ACC-08 capabilities.

findings.title: SPEC-01 tests cannot enforce DHF JSONB serialization policy without violating module boundaries
findings.evidence: "All wire formats and DHF JSONB payloads use camelCase property names... Both rules are enforced build-breaking in SPEC-01 tests."
findings.problem: SPEC-01 is defined as the protocol module, but the statement assigns enforcement of SPEC-04 DHF payload serialization to SPEC-01 tests.
findings.why_it_matters: Either SPEC-01 tests gain an undeclared dependency on SPEC-04, breaking the architecture, or the DHF serialization policy is not actually enforced where it is produced.
findings.proposed_fix: Split enforcement by ownership: keep wire-format serialization tests in SPEC-01 and move DHF JSONB serialization tests to SPEC-04 or a shared contract-test suite with explicit cross-module scope.

findings.title: Module boundaries are not concrete enough to implement the promised NetArchTest rules
findings.evidence: Module map uses "Lives In" values such as "`BSVoiceCAD.Addin`" and "`BSVoiceCAD.Orchestrator.Lifecycle` + `BSVoiceCAD.Addin.Bridge`"; Section 2 says arch rules live in "`BSVoiceCAD.Tests.Architecture`" and reference "all module assemblies."
findings.problem: The document mixes namespace-like labels with assembly-level enforcement language and does not specify which projects/assemblies actually constitute each module.
findings.why_it_matters: NetArchTest rules cannot be written deterministically until the module-to-assembly mapping is explicit, especially for SPEC-03 which is split across orchestrator and add-in bridge namespaces.
findings.proposed_fix: List the exact project/assembly names for each spec, or explicitly define the namespace sets and assembly boundaries that ArchTests must enforce.

findings.title: No top-level contract exists for turns that never reach completion
findings.evidence: "produces one DHF write per completed turn" / "one DHF entry per completed turn."
findings.problem: The document defines DHF behavior only for completed turns and does not state what happens to abandoned/in-flight turns during crash, disconnect, kill, or shutdown scenarios.
findings.why_it_matters: SPEC-03 and SPEC-04 can implement incompatible recovery behavior, and replay/integrity checks will be ambiguous when failures occur mid-turn.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the failure-path contract for incomplete turns: whether to append an aborted-turn record, emit a separate session event, or guarantee no record and how that is reconciled on restart/reconnect.

findings.title: LLM ownership is inconsistent after the SDR-TL-008 change
findings.evidence: "Opus 4.7 primary, Sonnet 4.6 for decoration extraction." / "Opus 4.7 plays two roles, not three. Vision interpreter ... and tool-calling agent."
findings.problem: The top-level contract no longer makes clear whether Sonnet 4.6 is still part of the runtime system, and "decoration extraction" is undefined here.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers cannot determine whether there is one model client path or multiple, which affects dependency injection, secrets/config, testing, and failure handling.
findings.proposed_fix: State explicitly whether Sonnet 4.6 remains in scope, which module owns it, and whether it is mandatory, stretch, or removed.

top_3_must_fix: Resolve the mandatory-vs-stretch contradiction for post-timeout recovery.
Resolve the mandatory-vs-stretch contradiction for screenshot/get_feature_tree grounding capabilities.
Define the integration/E2E test suite that owns the ACC scope gates.
